objective: Genuine short-time PDE existence via a semilinear parabolic mild-solution theorem: abstract Duhamel fixed-point (Banach contraction) on the Banach space C([0,T], E) for a heat-semigroup family S and Lipschitz nonlinearity F, with the concrete Gaussian-convolution bridge to D10/D11 on E = BCF(ℝⁿ). Identify derivative-loss/quasilinear barriers to Ricci-DeTurck; never assume the target existence theorem.

architecture.choice: abstract semilinear parabolic Duhamel fixed point + concrete Gaussian bridge
architecture.spatial_space: BCFn n = (EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n)) →ᵇ ℝ, the Banach space of bounded continuous functions on ℝⁿ with the uniform norm (Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.Bounded)
architecture.solution_space: Set.Icc (0:ℝ) T →ᵇ E, bounded continuous functions on the compact interval [0,T] with values in the spatial Banach space E (complete: BoundedContinuousFunction.instCompleteSpace)
architecture.duhamel_map: Φ(u)(t) = S t u₀ + ∫ s in 0..t, S (t - s) (F (u s)), Bochner interval integral
architecture.fixed_point: Mathlib.Topology.MetricSpace.ContractingWith (ContractingWith K f: K<1 ∧ LipschitzWith K f) + ContractingWith.fixedPoint on complete nonempty metric spaces
architecture.contraction_constant: K = M·L·T where ‖S t‖ ≤ M on [0,T], F is L-Lipschitz; contraction for T < 1/(M·L)
architecture.continuity_of_duhamel: Mathlib.MeasureTheory.Integral.DominatedConvergence.intervalIntegral.continuousAt_parametric_primitive_of_dominated (parameter-dependent interval integral continuity under joint continuity of the integrand and a constant domination bound)
architecture.why_not_ODE_relabeling: the Duhamel map uses the semigroup action S t on the initial datum AND S(t-s) on the nonlinearity, i.e. the true mild-solution structure; the Gaussian instance S t f = K_t * f is the heat convolution with the explicit D10 kernel, with the semigroup law K_t*K_s = K_{t+s} (D10, proved) and mass 1 (D10, proved). The abstract theorem is stated over a genuinely general interface S ≠ id.
architecture.ricci_deturck_barriers: named, not assumed: (i) derivative loss: the Duhamel fixed point only yields u ∈ C([0,T], E), no spatial derivative gain without a smoothing estimate; (ii) quasilinear regularity: DeTurck's g ↦ -2 Ric(g) + ∇*∇g is not globally Lipschitz on a fixed Banach space, so the Lipschitz hypothesis fails at the symbol level; (iii) strong continuity of K_t* on BUC and mild⇒classical differentiability are separate bridge obligations (Obligations.lean).
